display.purpose: Login and splash screens only. Never inside the authenticated app shell.

headline.purpose: Major section or page headings. Used sparingly.

title.purpose: Card headings, modal titles, sub-section labels.

body.purpose: All descriptive text, form hints, data cells. Max 70ch.

label.purpose: Form field legends, column headers, UI control labels.

amount.purpose: Every Rupiah figure. Always amber. Always tabular-nums.

shadows.name: hairline
shadows.purpose: Lightest definition. Companion to a thin border — use one or the other on static cards.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions. Snappy and decisive.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Color, border, and shadow transitions on interactive elements.

motion.name: duration-normal
motion.purpose: Enter animations (fade-up, scale-in) and panel transitions.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: Complex motion: slide-up sheets, modal entrances.

breakpoints.name: md

narrative.overview:
A point-of-sale is not a screen you admire — it's equipment you trust. Mass Laundry POS is built for counter staff who work under bright fluorescent light, tablet in hand, with a customer standing across from them. Every pixel earns its place by reducing decision time and eliminating doubt. The aesthetic is the visual equivalent of well-pressed linen: crisp, light, free of wrinkle.

The system's restraint is its confidence. One deep navy carries all primary actions. One warm amber singles out every price — you always know where the money is. Surfaces stay near-white with just enough tonal layering to establish hierarchy without contrast shock. JetBrains Mono for Rupiah figures makes amounts read like precision instruments.

What this system explicitly rejects: the dense gray chrome of legacy POS terminals; the gradients and mascots of consumer apps designed to entertain; the hero-metric templates and tracked-uppercase eyebrows of the SaaS dashboard monoculture; decorative animation or glassmorphism of any kind.
keyCharacteristics: Light theme, high contrast — legible under glare on any tablet display
Single-brand-color discipline: navy for action, amber for money, neutral for everything else
Touch-first: 44px minimum tap target, reachable from any hand position
Fast motion (150–220ms) that never blocks input; full reduced-motion support
Indonesian-first copy and Rupiah formatting as the default, not a translation layer

rules.name: The Gradient-for-Action Rule
rules.body: The navy→indigo gradient and indigo accent are reserved for action and emphasis: primary buttons, active nav, focus/selected states, hero headers, and headline metric tiles. Never as decoration on neutral content.

rules.name: The Amber-for-Money Rule
rules.body: The warm amber (--amount) is reserved exclusively for Rupiah amounts. The indigo accent never touches money. Using amber for non-financial emphasis is prohibited.

rules.name: The Light-Workspace Rule
rules.body: Data-entry surfaces (forms, tables, working cards) stay light and high-contrast. The dark navy chrome frames navigation and hero headers; it does not invade the workspace.

rules.name: The Cool-Neutral Rule
rules.body: All neutral surfaces and borders are tinted toward the brand's cool-blue hue. No cream, beige, or warm backgrounds.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Money Rule
rules.body: All Rupiah amounts render in JetBrains Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. No exceptions.

rules.name: The Scale Ceiling Rule
rules.body: No heading inside the authenticated app shell exceeds 1.875rem. Display sizes are for login/splash only.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any quantity, financial figure, order ID, or date column in a table uses font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards rest at Resting shadow. Shadow escalates only in response to interactive state. Decorative shadows on static elements are prohibited.

rules.name: The No-Ghost-Card Rule
rules.body: A 1px border and a box-shadow with blur ≥ 16px are never used together on the same element.

dos: Do use JetBrains Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums and the amber --amount token for every Rupiah figure.
Do keep motion to 150–220ms with cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1). Slower motion blocks perceived responsiveness.
Do include prefers-reduced-motion fallbacks for every animation and transition.
Do use min-height: 44px (touch spacing token) for all tappable elements.
Do apply env(safe-area-inset-*) padding to full-bleed mobile surfaces.
Do use text-ink (not text-ink-muted) for paragraph-length body copy.
Do use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on quantity, date, and ID columns in tables.
Do use the semantic z-index scale: base(0) raised(10) dropdown(200) sticky(300) overlay(400) modal(500) toast(600) tooltip(700).
donts: Don't use clunky legacy POS aesthetics: dense gray screens, tiny fonts, beveled buttons, Windows-era chrome.
Don't spray the navy→indigo gradient or indigo accent on neutral content (plain cards, body text, table rows, page backgrounds). It belongs on action and emphasis only.
Don't let dark chrome invade the workspace: forms, data tables, and working cards stay light. Dark is for navigation and hero framing.
Don't use the generic AI-dashboard template: identical icon-grid cards, gradient body text, or tracked-uppercase eyebrow kickers above every section.
Don't add overdesigned elements that slow data entry: glassmorphism, decorative backdrop-filter, heavy entrance choreography.
Don't pair a 1px border with a box-shadow of blur ≥ 16px on the same element.
Don't round cards beyond rounded-xl (16px) inside the app shell.
Don't use a warm, cream, or sand page background.
Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards or list items.
Don't introduce a third hue. The palette is navy + indigo (action/emphasis, as a gradient pair) and amber (money).
Don't use decorative shadows on static, non-interactive elements.
Don't exceed 1.875rem for headings inside the authenticated shell.
